To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
neonatal motoneurons and Renshaw interneurons survive the loss of their target neurons, but that the interneuronal phenotype changes with time.

interneuronal survival is target independent and that motoneuron axotomy induces transient changes in calcium-binding proteins in motoneurons and permanent changes in calcium-binding protein in interneurons.

(1) Interneurons in the ventral spinal cord are capable of surviving extensive motoneuron cell loss; (2) Motoneuron axotomy induces a transient up-regulation of CB in some motoneurons, but not in interneurons; and (3) Interneurons decrease CB expression after axotomy of their target motonuerons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and maintenance of calcium binding proteins in the nervous system and their role in the survival of motoneurons in amyotrophic laterals sclerosis.
the development of the motor system and the factors that contribute to its degeneration in amyotrophic sclerosis.
the mechanisms of neuronal death in the spinal cord.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interneurons are able to survive without their target motoneurones, but the loss of the target neurons does have an impact on the interneurones.
interneuronal survival is target dependent, but the loss of motoneuron target cells does not necessarily lead to the death of interneurons.
interneuronal survival in the absence of their target motonuerons is possible, but interneuronal function is altered as indicated by changes in CB expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

neonatal spinal motoneuron death is not a consequence of interneuronal degeneration but that interneurons may be capable of surviving in the absence of motoneurons, although their phenotype may change.
neonatal internuronal death is not a primary event in motoneuronal degeneration, but is secondary to loss of the target motoneuron.

interneuronal survival in response to motoneuronal death is dependent upon the age of the animal at the time of the insult and that the expression of calcium-binding proteins is altered in response to the loss of their target cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
interneuron survival is target independent.
the interneurons in the ventral horns of the spinal cord do not depend on the motoneurons for their survival, but they do change their phenotype.
interneurons are more robust than motoneurons in their ability to survive axotomy.
